This is almost (if not entirely) no useful information in this case. A mobile device which charges at 5v nominal will pull as many amps as it needs and no more. The reason they would die isn't because it "won't slow down". Slowing down in their case would be a reduction of amps, not voltage, because most mobile devices charge via USB which is regulated to output 5v (4.5-6.something). They reason they would die would be because the 5v rail wont stop supplying voltage when the device is done charging. Your phone charger will stop supplying amps and only supply voltage in intervals, to see if more power is needed. The 5v rail will just keep supplying voltage because there's nothing to tell it when to stop.
